notes: Most substantive pre-cutoff filing. Filing names DoD product families (MOJO, MIDS-JTRS, BFT, AMSS, Protected Tactical Service, TTNT, L-TAC, LACE) rather than PE numbers, so claims are mapped to the most likely Space Force / DoD SATCOM PEs in the J-Book corpus.

claims.claim_text: Viasat's government systems segment generated $1.36B in FY2024 (year ended March 31, 2024), 31.8% of total revenue ($4.28B), with U.S. DoD as primary customer; the company markets the segment as a growth pillar going forward.
claims.subject: Viasat government systems segment
claims.predicate: FY2024 revenue and forward growth narrative
claims.source_quote: Government systems Product 593,296 Service 770,846 Total 1,364,142 ... Total revenues $ 4,283,758. We believe that growth in our government systems business will be driven in the coming years by continued growth in demand for high-speed, high-quality, secure, resilient and reliable connectivity services ... to support government and military operations around the globe.

claims.claim_text: Viasat markets a Protected Tactical Service (PTS) field demonstration capability for the U.S. Air Force / Space Force as part of its government SATCOM offerings, with at least $45.3M obligated under FA880816C0005 (Protected Tactical Service field demonstration). Forward narrative implies continued positioning on the PTS production program of record.
claims.subject: Protected Tactical Service (PTS / PE 1206761SF) and Protected Tactical Enterprise Service (PTES / PE 1206760SF)
claims.predicate: named DoD program participation + forward exposure
claims.object_value: active PTS field-demo contract; positioned for follow-on
claims.source_quote: PROTECTED TACTICAL SERVICE FIELD DEMONSTRATION - VIASAT INC ... Our SATCOM systems, products and services are designed to support high-throughput broadband data links, to increase available bandwidth using existing satellite capacity, and to be resilient to withstand certain catastrophic events.

claims.claim_text: Inmarsat Government (acquired by Viasat May 2023) provides L-band narrowband SATCOM and Mobile User Objective System-class services to the DoD, including CONUS L-band and SPACE SEGMENT NA/SA awards totaling >$300M obligated historically. Forward narrative positions Inmarsat narrowband as material to the combined government systems business.
claims.subject: Narrowband Satellite Communications (PE 1203109SF) / L-band MILSATCOM
claims.predicate: named DoD program participation + forward L-band SATCOM exposure
claims.source_quote: Government Narrowband Products and Services (primarily provided by Inmarsat prior to the Inmarsat Acquisition), which provide military and government users with L-band products and services such as Tactical Beyond Line of Sight (L-TAC) communications, L-band airborne ISR services and L-band Advanced Communications Element (LACE) terminals.

claims.claim_text: Viasat positions its government SATCOM products (modems, terminals, network access control) for the Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS) and broader DoD commercial-augmentation market, leveraging multi-band terminals as part of the forward growth thesis.
claims.subject: Wideband Global SATCOM (PE 1206433SF) and Commercial SATCOM (PE 1206445SF)
claims.object_value: forward government SATCOM growth tied to WGS / COMSATCOM ecosystem
claims.source_quote: Government Satellite Communication (SATCOM) Systems, which offer an array of portable, mobile and fixed broadband modems, terminals, network access control systems and antenna systems using a range of satellite frequency bands for Command and Control (C2) missions, satellite networking services, and network management systems.

claims.claim_text: Viasat is a prime on MIDS-JTRS (Multifunctional Information Distribution System / Joint Tactical Radio System) terminals for the U.S. Navy, including N0003920F0291 ($58.4M) and N0003918F1373 ($50.4M); MIDS-JTRS is the primary Link-16 air/sea terminal of record. Forward exposure to Link-16 terminal demand is implied through MIDS deliveries even after the Link-16 TDL Business divestiture to L3Harris.
claims.subject: MIDS-JTRS terminals (Link-16 / Tactical Data Networks)
claims.source_quote: MIDS JTRS TERMINAL ... MIDS JTRS TERMINALS AND SPARES ... TACTICAL TARGETING NETWORK TECHNOLOGY (TTNT) SPECTRUM RELOCATION DEVELOPMENT DELIVERY ORDER.

claims.claim_text: Viasat sold the Link-16 TDL Business to L3Harris on January 3, 2023 for ~$1.96B, removing the Link-16 platform-of-record revenue stream from the go-forward government systems segment. Forward narrative does not claim ongoing Link-16 revenue, but the IDIQ relationships with DoD persist for MIDS terminals.
claims.subject: Link-16 TDL Business divestiture
claims.object_value: $1.96B sale price; Link-16 revenue no longer in continuing ops
claims.source_quote: On January 3, 2023, we completed the sale of certain assets and assigned liabilities comprising our Link-16 Tactical Data Links business (the Link-16 TDL Business) to L3Harris Technologies, Inc. (L3Harris) in exchange for approximately $1.96 billion in cash.

claims.claim_text: Viasat received the BFT2 (Blue Force Tracking) warranties / licenses contract HC108418C0002 ($136.2M) and AMSS III contract HC101318C0001 ($476.5M) — both large DISA-managed mobile-broadband program-of-record vehicles supporting forward government mobile broadband revenue.
claims.subject: BFT2 / AMSS III DISA program-of-record contracts
claims.predicate: named DoD program revenue + forward IDIQ exposure
claims.object_value: $612.7M combined obligated; forward MBSS / mobile broadband pipeline
claims.source_quote: IGF::OT::IGF AWARD FOR AMSS III ... BFT2 WARRANTIES/ LICENSES.

claims.claim_text: Viasat states its ability to execute its forward DoD strategy depends on continued growth of US government defense spending on space-based connectivity and resiliency, and explicitly warns that 'delays in approving U.S. Government budgets and cuts in government defense expenditures' are a material risk.
claims.subject: Forward US defense SATCOM spending environment
claims.predicate: macro DoD SATCOM funding direction at cutoff
claims.object_value: implied dependence on stable/growing SATCOM PE funding
claims.source_quote: delays in approving U.S. Government budgets and cuts in government defense expenditures; our reliance on U.S. Government contracts, and on a small number of contracts which account for a significant percentage of our revenues.

claims.claim_text: Viasat positions its small satellite development work as enabling a 'tactical space layer' for government customers — implicitly aligning with SDA-style proliferated-LEO programs (Tracking Layer, Transport Layer).
claims.subject: Small-satellite tactical space layer (SDA PWSA orbit)
claims.predicate: forward LEO tactical SATCOM pipeline exposure
claims.source_quote: Our small satellite development work is market leading and is designed to enable a new tactical space layer for our government customers, enabling increasingly advanced precision operations and maneuvering.

claims.claim_text: Viasat states its IR&D investments and patents underpin the proprietary technology behind both commercial and government SATCOM products, with patent litigation history (Acacia / Cisco $99.9M settlement in FY24) cited as evidence of enforceable IP.
